title: Bigtable: wide column, row key design and access patterns

videos.script: Quitanda's app sends a click for every screen a customer opens. Forty million on a busy day. {{stream}} Bigtable is built for that kind of stream. It is a sorted map. Every row has a key, and the rows are kept in the order of their keys. {{map}} Inside a row there are families, columns and cells. A column is just a name the program writes. And a cell keeps its old versions, until a policy says they can go. {{cells}} So the whole design is the row key. The customer first, then the time, reversed so the newest comes first. One customer's history is then one short read. {{key}} Put the time first instead, and every new click goes to the same end of the table. One node does the work while the others wait. {{hotspot}} Then the bill. Bigtable charges for nodes by the hour, busy or idle. {{nodes}} The emulator stores and sorts, and that is all. Nodes, tablets and the heat map of a hot key are read here from Google's documentation. {{emulator}}
